# Conclusion

The stakes are high. The alternative to a life of wisdom is not mediocrity or monotony. The foolish, simple, and naive do not just face a mere lackluster and bland existence. Outside of wisdom is peril and disaster. In the end, there are only two ways to live: wisdom in the fear of God or folly bound up with human depravity. In this same way, there are only two ways to parent: leading our children onto the righteous paths that lead to life or leading them astray on the wicked paths that lead to destruction. Our civic involvement and vocations will take on a certain kind of quality: establishing God's justice or contributing to the world's unraveling. Church leadership and ministry finds itself at a similar crossroads: promoting godliness or promulgating godlessness (even if under the guise of pseudo-spiritualities). May we heed the voice of Solomon to his son, ingesting this truth as a certain guide for our personal faith, family rule, vocational pursuits, and engagement with the world.
